_comment: Big Five → 19 domain trait derivation coefficients for BigFiveAdapter. Formula: value = 0.5 + sum_{bf in OCEAN}(coeff_bf * (bf_score - 0.5)), clamped to [0,1]. Each trait entry cites its literature source with DOI where available and a confidence marker (high/moderate/low). Traits omitted from this table fall back to 0.5 — this is explicit, NOT a bug. Coefficients are literature-informed best estimates, NOT measured correlations on a REALM-specific sample; report validity-study results against a held-out trait inventory before claiming predictive accuracy.
_formula: value = 0.5 + sum(coeff_bf * (bf_score - 0.5)) for bf in {openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, neuroticism}; clamp to [0, 1]

_confidence_legend.high: Direct facet/aspect loading from a primary source; construct near-identical to REALM trait.
_confidence_legend.moderate: Composite derivation from multiple partial correlations, or mapping from closely-related but non-identical construct.
_confidence_legend.low: Translated from a near-synonym or single weak-magnitude study. Validity study may show weak performance — framed explicitly, not retroactively.

_sources.Zhao_Seibert_2006: Zhao, H., & Seibert, S. E. (2006). The big five personality dimensions and entrepreneurial status: A meta-analytical review. Journal of Applied Psychology, 91(2), 259-271. DOI: 10.1037/0021-9010.91.2.259
_sources.Lauriola_Levin_2001: Lauriola, M., & Levin, I. P. (2001). Personality traits and risky decision-making in a controlled experimental task: An exploratory study. Personality and Individual Differences, 31(2), 215-226. DOI: 10.1016/S0191-8869(00)00130-6
_sources.Costa_McCrae_1992: Costa, P. T. Jr., & McCrae, R. R. (1992). Revised NEO Personality Inventory (NEO-PI-R) and NEO Five-Factor Inventory (NEO-FFI): Professional Manual. Odessa, FL: Psychological Assessment Resources.
_sources.DeYoung_Quilty_Peterson_2007: DeYoung, C. G., Quilty, L. C., & Peterson, J. B. (2007). Between facets and domains: 10 aspects of the Big Five. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 93(5), 880-896. DOI: 10.1037/0022-3514.93.5.880

_excluded_by_design.political_spectrum: See data/astro/planet_trait_map.json:_excluded_by_design. REALM models personality temperament, not ideological preference. Scope boundary applies uniformly across input adapters — the BigFive layer also deliberately does not parameterize political orientation.

_unsourced_traits.herd_susceptibility: No published Big Five correlation found for this trait. Weakly speculated links to Agreeableness (compliance) or Neuroticism (anxiety-driven conformity) exist but lack clean empirical derivation. Fallback to 0.5.
_unsourced_traits.fomo_susceptibility: No published Big Five correlation found for this trait. Recent FOMO scales post-date NEO development and haven't been cross-validated against Big Five. Fallback to 0.5.
_unsourced_traits.individualism: Individualism is a cultural dimension (Hofstede IDV), not a Big Five construct. Use DemographicAdapter for culture-derived individualism. Fallback to 0.5 in BigFive path.
_unsourced_traits.tradition_vs_progress: Cultural/ideological dimension, not Big Five. NEO Openness.Values is weak and contested for this mapping. Fallback to 0.5.
_unsourced_traits.spirituality: No robust Big Five correlation. NEO Openness.Values and Openness.Aesthetics show weak, culture-dependent links but not sufficient for derivation. Fallback to 0.5.

risk_appetite.source: Zhao_Seibert_2006 (entrepreneurs higher O, lower N/A); Lauriola_Levin_2001 (Openness strongest trait-level predictor of risk-taking in experimental lottery tasks). Primary facet loadings: E5 Excitement-Seeking (Zuckerman sensation-seeking) drives the E+ path; N5 Impulsiveness carries the within-N positive component that offsets anxiety-driven risk aversion; C6 Cautiousness is the inverse-C facet (high cautiousness suppresses risk appetite).
risk_appetite.note: Meta-analytic entrepreneurial-risk findings (Zhao-Seibert) converge with experimental risk-taking correlations (Lauriola-Levin). Composite; no single study reports all five coefficients. The C- loading reflects entrepreneurial risk-tolerance, which runs counter to the general-population C↔caution link. Facet refinement (Sprint 6): E5 Excitement-Seeking, N5 Impulsiveness, C6 Cautiousness are the carrying facets on their respective domains.

analytical_depth.source: Costa_McCrae_1992 (NEO-PI-R facets O5 Ideas, C6 Deliberation)
analytical_depth.note: O.Ideas measures intellectual curiosity and appetite for analysis; C.Deliberation measures careful thought before action. Both facets load near-cleanly on their domain, so large coefficients are justified.

impulsivity.source: Costa_McCrae_1992 (N5 Impulsiveness is the canonical Big-Five impulsivity facet; E5 Excitement-Seeking contributes the E+ path via reward-driven behavioral activation; C6 Cautiousness is the inverse-C facet whose low pole characterizes impulsive action).
impulsivity.note: N5 Impulsiveness is Costa-McCrae's eponymous facet — inability to resist cravings/urges. E+ via E5 Excitement-Seeking. C- via C6 Cautiousness (anti-Deliberation). Sprint 6: E6 Cheerfulness citation removed — Johnson IPIP-NEO-120 data shows r(E6, impulsivity_synth) = -0.265, opposite sign from REALM's E+ coefficient. The E domain effect on impulsivity runs through E5, not E6.

patience.source: Costa_McCrae_1992 (C5 Self-Discipline; conceptual inverse of N5 Impulsiveness)
patience.note: Patience derived as conceptual inverse of impulsivity: C.Self-Discipline primary positive loading, N- and E- mirror the impulsivity mapping.

social_dominance.source: DeYoung_Quilty_Peterson_2007 (BFAS Extraversion.Assertiveness aspect negatively correlates with Agreeableness.Politeness)
social_dominance.note: Assertiveness is the canonical dominance construct in BFAS. Politeness is the anti-dominance agreeableness aspect. Direct aspect loadings.

empathy.note: Tender-Mindedness measures sympathy/concern for others — construct-closest to empathy. Small N+ reflects anxious-empathic subtype (emotional contagion). Pure A loading would understate the N-linked sensitivity.

loss_aversion.source: Lauriola_Levin_2001 (Neuroticism associates with loss-oriented framing in lottery experiments; Extraversion effect stronger in gain than loss contexts). Primary facet loadings: N1 Anxiety and N3 Depression carry the N+ path (loss-framing sensitivity is amplified by anxiety and negative affect); C6 Cautiousness contributes the C+ path (risk-avoidance orientation); E5 Excitement-Seeking contributes the inverse-E path (high sensation-seekers are less loss-averse).
loss_aversion.note: Lauriola-Levin report partial correlations in experimental tasks rather than a full personality-loss-aversion meta-analysis. Coefficients are the authors' directional findings scaled to REALM's additive range. Facet refinement (Sprint 6): N1 Anxiety, N3 Depression, C6 Cautiousness, E5 Excitement-Seeking (inverse) are the carrying facets.

financial_optimism.source: Costa_McCrae_1992 (E6 Positive-Emotion; inverse of N3 Depression)
financial_optimism.note: Financial optimism mapped to general trait optimism: E.Positive-Emotion primary, minus N.Depression. Small O+ for openness-to-upside-scenarios.

communication_assertiveness.note: Direct aspect loading. Mild A- reflects willingness to push back / occupy airtime in conversation, which trades against Politeness.

persuasion_skill.note: Persuasion combines assertiveness (airtime) with warmth/enthusiasm (likability). Mild A+ reflects warm-persuasion style; mild O+ for cognitive flexibility in framing arguments.

information_sharing.note: No direct construct in the Big-Five literature. Composite of E.Gregariousness (interaction frequency) + O.Ideas (enjoyment of intellectual exchange). A+ small contribution for prosocial sharing orientation.

contrarian_tendency.note: Contrarian behavior anti-correlates with A.Compliance but there is no dedicated Big-Five contrarianism study. Low confidence — treat as directional derivation only, subject to validity-study re-measurement.

authority_compliance.source: Costa_McCrae_1992 (A4 Compliance, C3 Dutifulness); NEO O.Values inverse
authority_compliance.note: Authority compliance is heavily culturally-driven (cf. Hofstede PDI), not primarily a Big-Five construct. Low-confidence derivation — use DemographicAdapter when authority compliance is a focus.

_facet_formula: When use_facets=true AND all required facets are provided: value = 0.5 + sum(facet_coeff * (facet_score - 0.5)) over the trait's facet_coefficients; clamp to [0, 1]. Unlisted facets contribute 0. Falls back to domain formula otherwise.
